value.author: samMularczyk
value.layerInfo: Film in one node: halation, tone roll-off, grain, a Fujifilm-style colour recipe and projector wear.

halation: Warm bloom from light scattering back through the film base, spreading around highlights.
halationRadius: How far the halation spreads, in pixels. The layer bounds expand to match.
halationThreshold: Luminance above which highlights start to glow. Softly thresholded, so the matte has no hard edge.
halationDensity: How much denser the core of the glow is than its falloff. Higher makes only the brightest highlights bloom.
halationTint: Which channels the scatter shows up in. The original used a deep orange, so it lands mostly in red.
linearise: Applies a 2.2 transfer before the tone curve and undoes it after. Off by default - Cavalry has its own colour management.
exposure: Stops of gain before the tone curve. This is what drives highlights into the roll-off.
rolloff: Compresses highlights through a filmic shoulder. It needs something above white to compress, so raise Exposure or Halation first - on a plain 0-1 image it has nothing to work on and only lifts the midtones.
gamutExtension: Width of the gamut the roll-off happens inside. Wider desaturates highlights further before they clip.
recipe: Strength of the Recipe tab's Fujifilm-style grade. 0 leaves colour untouched.
base: Starting colour character, built from published descriptions of a film simulation. Mono and Mono Flat are black and white.
colour: Overall saturation trim, on Fujifilm's -4 to +4 scale.
highlightTone: Density of the highlights, -2 to +4. Positive is harder, negative softer.
shadowTone: Density of the shadows, -2 to +4. Positive crushes them, negative opens them up.
highlightProtect: Highlight protection, as the camera's DR100 / DR200 / DR400. Higher holds the top end back.
colourChrome: Deepens colours that are already saturated, leaving pale ones alone. Off, Weak (0.5) or Strong (1.0).
colourChromeBlue: The same, restricted to blues and cyans - for skies and deep blues specifically.
wbShiftR: Red trim on Fujifilm's white balance shift grid, -9 to +9.
wbShiftB: Blue trim on the same grid. Positive is cooler, negative warmer.
monoToning: Warm or cool cast for the black and white bases, matching MonochromaticColor. No effect on the colour bases.
clarity: Local contrast, -5 to +5: micro-contrast without touching overall tone. Negative softens the way a diffusion filter does.
clarityRadius: Size of the detail Clarity acts on, in pixels. Small values sharpen fine texture, large values shape broad areas.
grain: Film grain strength (k in the signal-dependent model x + k*x^gamma*u).
grainSize: Size of one grain in pixels.
grainBlur: Texture of the grain field: 0 is soft organic clumps, 1 is fine correlated noise.
grainResponse: Signal-dependent amplification exponent - lower makes grain rise faster with brightness.
grainDomain: Whether grain is added before or after the tone curve. Positive Print grains the developed image; Negative grains before it, so the curve reshapes the grain too.
scannerNoise: Separate white noise modelling a telecine/scanner's own sensor noise, independent of film grain.
time: Driven by the composition time. Disconnect it to freeze the film artefacts.
damage: Strength of the Damage tab's projector wear. 0 is a pristine print.
damageDomain: Whether dirt, scratches, vignette and flicker are applied to the print or to the (inverted) negative, which changes how they land in highlights versus shadows.
frameRate: Steps time to this rate for a projected-film judder. Zero leaves motion smooth.
speed: How fast the damage clock runs relative to real time. 1 is real time; lower slows the judder and weave, higher speeds them up.
weave: How much the picture wanders in the gate, as a fraction of the layer. A mean-reverting wander rather than a steady drift.
flicker: Frame-to-frame exposure wobble, log-normal like a real lamp/shutter flicker rather than symmetric.
dirtThreshold: How much dirt shows. Lower values let more specks and scratches through.
dirtScale: Size of the dirt features. Lower values give finer specks.
scratches: Density of vertical gate scratches - thin, flickering, drifting sideways over time.
scratchWidth: Base width of a scratch in pixels. Real scratches are thin - keep this small.
vignetteFlicker: How much the vignette breathes over time.
desaturate: One is full black and white, as in the original. Lower it to keep some colour.
amount: Mix between the original layer and the film result.
